envelope.text: ///   POSIX row). They ride on the [`Context`] in argv order and are applied

why:
phase-482 W5 (2026-10-07) -- THE RESIDUE LANDED, and the row leaves `gap`. `-p`/`--param [node:]name:=value` and `--params-file <path>` are honoured when `nros` has `param-services` (RFC-0015 section 9's POSIX row): parsed by `nros_node::ros_args::parse_ros_args_events`, files read with `std::fs` and parsed by `parse_params_yaml`, carried on the `Context`, installed by `Context::create_executor` (`Executor::install_argv_params`), and applied when a node DECLARES the parameter -- the last matching override wins, typed by the declared default. `adopt-bounded`, with the envelope stated in `init_with_args`'s doc: scalars only from a file, a node key matched by NAME, and a value that does not parse as the declared type logged with the default kept (RFC-0015 section 9.6). Without a parameter store the flags are still refused by name. The C++ twin is `nros_cpp_install_argv_remaps` (`apply_ros_args_with_params`).

Before phase-482 W5: phase-467 Row 11 (2026-10-03) -- THE PARSE LANDED, and the row stays `gap` for exactly ONE residue: parameter overrides (`-p`/`--param`/`--params-file`), recorded in `owed` with a witness. Everything the row owed before -- the `--ros-args` parse, and the `-r`/`--remap` remap rules it carries -- is shipped. One parse (`parse_ros_args_or_refuse`, `packages/api/nros/src/init.rs`) serves this name and its twin `rust:Context::new`.

WHY STILL `gap` AND NOT `divergence`. SCHEMA.md (issue 1463): "a behaviour bound that is PERMANENT is not a `gap` at all -- it is a `divergence` with its constraint." The `-p` refusal is NOT permanent: RFC-0015 section 9 designs the runtime-parameter channel and its section 9.6 is open, and when it lands this parser is its POSIX producer. Calling the row closed while a porting user's `-p foo:=42` is still refused would be the stale closure 1463 was filed about. The OTHER bounds below ARE permanent (identity remaps: build-time freeze, RFC-0046; freestanding: no argv), and would make the row a `divergence` on their own once `-p` lands.

UPSTREAM'S CONTRACT: `rclcpp::init(argc, argv)` / rclrs `Context::new(args, ..)` hand the process arguments to `rcl_parse_arguments` (Humble `rcl/arguments.h`): ROS arguments between `--ros-args` and `--` (or the end), several scopes allowed, `-r`/`--remap [node:]from:=to` rules kept in argv order, `-p`/`--param` overrides, and rclcpp throws `UnknownROSArgsError` for any ROS argument rcl left unparsed. rclrs has no free `init_with_args`; this name is ours (the C++-symmetric anchor beside `init()`), so the key correlates `ours-only`.

OURS: `init_with_args(args)` parses with rcl's grammar (`nros_node::ros_args::parse_ros_args`, `packages/core/nros-node/src/ros_args.rs`) and returns a `Context` carrying the `-r` rules in a private field. `Context::create_executor` / `create_executor_in` install them in the executor's remap table tagged as the FALLBACK tier of `nros_node::names::resolve_name_layered` (PR #1523). From there they reach entities on every road that resolves names: `Executor::resolve_entity_name_for` (the C and C++ APIs), `ExecutorSink::create_entity` (`nros::node!` components, via `nros_node::ros_args::argv_fallback`), and the handle `Executor::create_node` returns -- which before this consulted NO remap at all, so a rule declared on the executor already missed every entity created through it.

THE PRECEDENCE RULE, decided by PR #1523 and now exercised with a real producer: LAUNCH IS AUTHORITATIVE; an argv rule applies only to a name the launch projected no rule for. RFC-0046's ruling for node identity, applied to remaps -- and rcl's own arrangement: `rcl_remap_topic_name` checks a node's LOCAL arguments (how launch and component containers hand a node its rules) and only on no match the GLOBAL ones `rcl_init` received (Humble `rcl/remap.h`). Within argv, the first rule wins (`foo:=bar bar:=baz` sends `foo` to `bar`), as rcl documents.

ADOPT-BOUNDED -- THE ENVELOPE, stated in the doc comment. Everything below is REFUSED LOUDLY at the call (logged through `nros_log`, then a panic carrying `REFUSE_INIT_ARGS` and the offending argument), never skipped:
  * `-p` / `--param` / `--params-file` -- THE OWED RESIDUE (see `owed`). Not built here because RFC-0015 section 9 owns the runtime-parameter channel (`nros_runtime_args_get`, `apply_runtime_param_overrides`, "writes into the same parameter store that ~/set_parameters reads") and its section 9.6 is still open; a second answer built on this row would pre-empt that RFC. It also does not fit this carrier: a remap is consulted when an entity is NAMED, a parameter override when a parameter is DECLARED, into a store that is image-wide (#1408) and would need its own executor table and sizing. When section 9 lands, `-p` is that channel's POSIX producer, using this parser, and this row becomes a `divergence`.
  * Node-identity remaps (`__node`, `__name`, `__ns`, any `__` rule). PLATFORM CONSTRAINT: an image's node identity is frozen at build time (RFC-0015 section 2.1) and launch-authoritative (RFC-0046), which has no argv rung.
  * `rostopic://` / `rosservice://` rules (rcl's own header marks them unfinished), `-e`/`--enclave`, the log flags, and any token inside a scope that is not a ROS flag.
  * The FREESTANDING half: the name is `cfg(feature = "env")`, absent on an image with no argv.

WHERE THE RULES DO NOT REACH, measured and stated rather than discovered: (1) `Context::config` cannot carry them into the `ExecutorConfig` `Executor::open` takes, so it REFUSES a context that has any (`config_refuses_a_context_that_carries_remaps`). (2) Entities registered through the executor's own `add_*` methods or a `node_mut` context are not remapped, because those are also where the C ABI and the component sink hand ALREADY-RESOLVED names -- remapping there would apply a rule twice, and `a:=b b:=c` would then send `a` to `c`, which rcl forbids. Splitting the user-facing entry from the post-resolution sink is the follow-up that would close (2). (3) A `nros sync` image reads no argv: its entry builds its own `RuntimeCtx` and never reaches `init_with_args`, consistent with RFC-0015 section 9.2, which classes topic remaps as graph topology for exactly those images.

TESTS. Parser: 10 in `ros_args.rs` (scopes, both flag spellings, node prefix, refusals by name). Chain -- real argv, parsed, installed, resolved: `a_launch_rule_wins_over_argv_even_when_argv_was_installed_first` (declaration order argues for the wrong winner), `an_argv_rule_applies_where_the_launch_projected_none`, `a_node_prefixed_argv_rule_reaches_only_that_node`, `within_argv_the_first_rule_wins`, `argv_fallback_yields_only_argv_rules_for_the_named_node`, `install_is_all_or_nothing`. NodeHandle, asserted on the name the BACKEND received: `create_node_handle_applies_an_argv_remap`, `create_node_handle_prefers_a_launch_rule_over_argv`, `create_node_handle_passes_an_unmatched_name_through_unchanged`. Context: `remap_rules_ride_on_the_context_in_argv_order`, `parameter_overrides_are_still_refused_by_name`, `identity_remaps_are_refused`, `context_new_parses_exactly_like_init_with_args`. Mutation-checked: dropping the fallback tier from the C/C++ resolver fails 3; flattening the table to first-match regardless of tier fails 3; making the handle consult no remap fails 2.

HISTORY. Recorded `gap` + `refuse-loud` from phase-427 W9, when the parameter was `_args` and `--ros-args -p foo:=42` had been silently discarded; re-dispositioned `adopt-bounded` on 2026-09-23 to match its twin. phase-467's study asked whether argv remaps should override launch-projected ones; PR #1317 measured that launch remaps are never projected into the environment at all (they are emitted into the generated entry), and PR #1523 landed the two-tier resolution and the precedence rule with an empty fallback, correcting the study's prescription, which had named the C/C++ store as if it were the only one.
